_meta.indication: Treatment of wounds associated with dystrophic and junctional epidermolysis bullosa in adult and pediatric patients 6 months of age and older.

pivotal_trials.population: Adults and pediatric subjects 6 months of age and older with dystrophic or junctional epidermolysis bullosa
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of subjects with first complete closure of the EB target wound within 45 days
pivotal_trials.result: First complete closure of target wound within 45 days: 41.3% FILSUVEZ vs 28.9% placebo (95% CI for treatment difference 0.8, 25.6); unadjusted p=0.041, adjusted p=0.013

key_safety: The most common (incidence ≥2%) adverse reactions are application site reactions (7.3% FILSUVEZ vs 6.1% placebo). Local hypersensitivity and skin reactions, including urticaria and dermatitis, have been reported.
target_moa: Birch triterpenes is a botanical drug substance composed of a mixture of pentacyclic triterpenes (mainly betulin) derived from birch bark; the mechanism of action in the treatment of EB wounds is unknown.
modality: Other (botanical drug substance / topical gel of birch triterpenes)

advisory_committee.vote: No Advisory Committee meeting was convened in response to this application.
